title: How Does the Stomach Know Food Is Coming?

scenes.visual: Title card 'How Does the Stomach Know Food Is Coming?' over the first film's left-to-right tube. Reuses the first film's COLOUR MAP: food GREY, water BLUE, microbes GREEN, acid and gastric juice GOLD, blood RED, lacteal PALE YELLOW. New for this film: nerves WHITE lines, hormones small PURPLE dots carried in RED blood. Every number appears only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: How does a stomach know a meal is coming? Can it start work before any food arrives?
scenes.visual: The tube with an empty GOLD-tinted stomach. A cartoon bowl of meat appears near the mouth; a small clock beside the stomach ticks, label 'ready yet?'.
scenes.narration: How does a stomach know a meal is coming? Can it start work before any food arrives?

scenes.tts: The first film showed the gut as a one-way line, with several stretches working at once. Some signals ready a stretch before food arrives. Others answer once it is there.
scenes.visual: Brief replay of the first film's tube: GREY blocks fill several stations at once, 'mouth', 'stomach', 'duodenum', 'small intestine'. The stomach lights up before any block reaches it (label 'before'); the duodenum lights up as blocks arrive (label 'on arrival').
scenes.narration: The first film showed the gut as a one-way line, with several stretches working at once. Some signals ready a stretch before food arrives. Others answer once it is there.

scenes.tts: Ivan Pavlov's laboratory, in Saint Petersburg, asked this of dogs. The dogs had recovered from surgery, and were awake and eating. So one gland at a time could be studied in a whole, living animal.
scenes.visual: Caption 'Ivan Pavlov's laboratory, St Petersburg'. A cartoon dog stands at a bowl, healthy and alert. Schematic drawing, not a historical image.
scenes.narration: Ivan Pavlov's laboratory, in Saint Petersburg, asked this of dogs. The dogs had recovered from surgery, and were awake and eating. So one gland at a time could be studied in a whole, living animal.

scenes.tts: In one dog, the esophagus was opened at the neck. Food the dog swallowed fell out into a dish. It never reached the stomach.
scenes.visual: Cutaway of the dog: the esophagus drawn as a tube from mouth to stomach, broken at the neck. GREY food chunks travel down from the mouth and drop out of the neck opening into a dish. The stomach below stays empty.
scenes.narration: In one dog, the esophagus was opened at the neck. Food the dog swallowed fell out into a dish. It never reached the stomach.

scenes.tts: A second opening, called a fistula, let the workers collect juice straight from the stomach into a flask.
scenes.visual: A short tube from the stomach wall leads out of the body to an empty glass flask, label 'gastric fistula'. The flask is clearly empty.
scenes.narration: A second opening, called a fistula, let the workers collect juice straight from the stomach into a flask.

scenes.tts: Suppose stomach juice flows only when food touches the stomach. What should the flask collect while this dog eats?
scenes.visual: The dog eats; GREY chunks keep falling into the neck dish. A question card appears beside the flask.
scenes.narration: Suppose stomach juice flows only when food touches the stomach. What should the flask collect while this dog eats?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds beside the empty flask; 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: After a delay of some minutes, acid juice flowed. It came from the stomach, through the fistula. The dog was eating, but no food had reached its stomach.
scenes.visual: A small clock spins forward, label 'some minutes'. Then GOLD drops run from the stomach down the fistula tube and collect in the flask. The stomach is still empty of GREY food.
scenes.narration: After a delay of some minutes, acid juice flowed. It came from the stomach, through the fistula. The dog was eating, but no food had reached its stomach.

scenes.tts: Then both vagus nerves were cut. These nerves run from the brainstem to the stomach. Now the dog ate, and the flask stayed empty.
scenes.visual: Two WHITE lines run from a small brainstem shape down to the stomach, labelled 'vagus nerves'. Scissors snip both lines. The dog eats again; food falls into the neck dish; the flask stays dry.
scenes.narration: Then both vagus nerves were cut. These nerves run from the brainstem to the stomach. Now the dog ate, and the flask stayed empty.

scenes.tts: So in the dog, nerves start the stomach early. This is the cephalic phase, set off by the sight, smell, taste and chewing of food.
scenes.visual: Uncut WHITE vagus lines flash from brain to stomach while icons for 'sight', 'smell', 'taste' and 'chewing' sit near the dog's head. Label 'cephalic phase (in the dog: needs the vagus)'.
scenes.narration: So in the dog, nerves start the stomach early. This is the cephalic phase, set off by the sight, smell, taste and chewing of food.

scenes.tts: This rules in a nerve-driven start. It does not rule out later steps, once food is inside the gut.
scenes.visual: Two labels side by side: 'ruled in: nerves start the stomach' with a tick, and 'not ruled out: later steps' with an open box. The tube from the opening returns.
scenes.narration: This rules in a nerve-driven start. It does not rule out later steps, once food is inside the gut.

scenes.tts: Here are two later steps. Chyme, the stomach's acid soup of food, moves on into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine.
scenes.visual: Back on the tube. A GOLD-tinged mass labelled 'chyme' squeezes from the stomach into the duodenum.
scenes.narration: Here are two later steps. Chyme, the stomach's acid soup of food, moves on into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine.

scenes.tts: These steps use hormones. A hormone is a substance released into the blood, which acts on distant target cells. The blood carries the message to the next gland.
scenes.visual: Close-up of the duodenal wall beside a RED capillary. A single PURPLE dot leaves a wall cell, enters the RED stream and rides it away toward a distant gland outline, label 'hormone: released into blood, acts at a distance'.
scenes.narration: These steps use hormones. A hormone is a substance released into the blood, which acts on distant target cells. The blood carries the message to the next gland.

scenes.tts: Acid arriving there makes the duodenal lining release a hormone, secretin, into the blood. The pancreas answers with fluid rich in bicarbonate, which neutralizes the acid.
scenes.visual: Cells of the duodenal wall release PURPLE dots labelled 'secretin' into a RED capillary. The RED vessel carries them to the pancreas, which sends fluid labelled 'bicarbonate' back into the duodenum; the GOLD tint fades to neutral.
scenes.narration: Acid arriving there makes the duodenal lining release a hormone, secretin, into the blood. The pancreas answers with fluid rich in bicarbonate, which neutralizes the acid.

scenes.tts: Fat and protein arriving release a second hormone, cholecystokinin, called C C K. The pancreas sends enzymes, and the gallbladder squeezes out bile.
scenes.caption: Fat and protein arriving release a second hormone, cholecystokinin, called CCK. The pancreas sends enzymes, and the gallbladder squeezes out bile.
scenes.visual: Grains labelled 'fat' and 'protein' arrive in the duodenum. The wall releases PURPLE dots labelled 'CCK' into RED blood. The pancreas sends a stream labelled 'enzymes'; the gallbladder visibly contracts and squirts a stream labelled 'bile' into the duodenum.
scenes.narration: Fat and protein arriving release a second hormone, cholecystokinin, called CCK. The pancreas sends enzymes, and the gallbladder squeezes out bile.

scenes.tts: So nerves start the stomach before food arrives. And a stretch that food has just reached signals the glands that serve it. The duodenum reports acid, fat and protein, and the right glands answer.
scenes.visual: Recap strip: WHITE vagus lines to the stomach with the dog's flask filling; PURPLE secretin and CCK dots travelling in RED blood from the duodenum to the pancreas and gallbladder.
scenes.narration: So nerves start the stomach before food arrives. And a stretch that food has just reached signals the glands that serve it. The duodenum reports acid, fat and protein, and the right glands answer.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex. LINE: 'Nerves ready the stomach early; hormones answer food as it arrives.'
